convention: The same three-state convention as messages/lg.needs-translation.json, for the Prescriptions namespace: a key is translated, awaiting a translator, or identical on purpose. Every key under needsTranslation below holds the ENGLISH text verbatim, because the agent that wrote this namespace does not speak Luganda and this namespace is DOSING INSTRUCTIONS. A confident-sounding wrong translation of how much of a medicine to take, or of the sentence saying a prescription was cancelled, is worse than an honest English string a reader can recognise as foreign and ask a relative or a pharmacist about. src/i18n/i18n.test.ts checks only the BASE catalogues, so nothing enforces this file; it is a worklist for a translator, not a gate.
translateFirst: Prescriptions.cancelledTitle and Prescriptions.cancelledBody, then Prescriptions.controlledNote and Prescriptions.itemsMissingBody. The first pair is the sentence that stops somebody taking a medicine the clinic has withdrawn. The second pair prevents two specific wrong actions: expecting a controlled medicine to be delivered, and reading a failed load of the item list as "nothing was prescribed". Prescriptions.directionsLabel and the four item labels around it are short and high-frequency and should be done in the same pass, because they head the text a patient actually doses from.

translated.Prescriptions.itemsHeading: Eddagala — the ordinary Luganda word for medicine. Short, unambiguous, and already used on the Delivery screen for the same thing.
